decision.question: Should the Retry-After upper bound be a new optional `Retry.__init__` parameter (e.g. `retry_after_max: float | None`) that defaults to `None` (unbounded, i.e. identical to current behavior), rather than a parameter with a finite default or a global/module-level setting?
decision.context:
src/urllib3/util/retry.py:202-245 `Retry.__init__` currently has no cap on Retry-After; `sleep_for_retry` (line 335-341) sleeps for the full parsed `Retry-After` value with no limit. `backoff_max` (DEFAULT_BACKOFF_MAX=120, line 196-197, 213, 237) is the existing precedent for a similarly-named cap, but it applies only to the exponential-backoff path, not to Retry-After. Task requires the change not unexpectedly alter existing retry behavior for callers who don't opt in, so the new knob must default to a no-op (None/unbounded) to preserve compatibility for library-next.
Paths: src/urllib3/util/retry.py
Options: New optional constructor parameter `retry_after_max` defaulting to None (no cap unless caller opts in) -- preserves all existing behavior by default, matches `backoff_max` naming convention | Give it a finite default (e.g. same as backoff_max=120) -- would silently cap Retry-After sleeps for all existing callers, changing current behavior unexpectedly | Only expose it as a `sleep()`/`sleep_for_retry()` call-time argument rather than a Retry constructor field -- inconsistent with how `respect_retry_after_header` and `backoff_max` are already configured on Retry
decision.routing_reason: Referred to Engineer a9717c by Engineer 654255
decision.answer: Use a new optional retry_after_max constructor argument in seconds. Default it to None so existing callers are unchanged. A finite limit must be opt-in, not a global default. This is my decision for library-next.
decision.rationale: No separate rationale recorded; any reason is included in the complete authored answer.
decision.owner_evidence: handed on by Engineer 654255: "Could you ask <@UC6A9ECF3F4> instead? They maintain runtime retry behavior."
